name: ToolGen: Unified Tool Retrieval and Calling via Generation
venue: ICLR 2025 (arXiv:2410.03439, submitted Oct 2024, last revised Mar 2025; DBLP: conf/iclr/WangHJWB025; OpenReview id XLMAMmowdY)
authors_affiliation: Renxi Wang (LibrAI; MBZUAI - Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence); Xudong Han (LibrAI; MBZUAI); Lei Ji (Microsoft); Shu Wang (UCLA - University of California, Los Angeles); Timothy Baldwin (LibrAI; MBZUAI; The University of Melbourne); Haonan Li (LibrAI; MBZUAI). Primary affiliation: MBZUAI / LibrAI.
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/Reason-Wang/ToolGen (official author repo; not a continuously-maintained leaderboard) [uncertain]
task_domain: Tool-use: large-scale LLM-agent tool/API retrieval and calling. Unifies tool retrieval and autonomous task completion (tool invocation + argument generation) over a pool of 47k real-world APIs (ToolBench / RapidAPI).
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent tool-use with full-parameter supervised fine-tuning of an open LLM (Llama-3-8B). Given a user query and a tool repository of 16k+ tools / 47k unique APIs, the agent must (1) retrieve the correct tool(s) and (2) iteratively complete the task by generating Thought -> Action (tool) -> Arguments and consuming tool feedback over multiple turns. Supervision comes from ToolBench-derived (query, relevant-API) pairs and trajectory data. Unlike the standard retriever-then-LLM pipeline, ToolGen folds retrieval into the LLM's next-token generation by expanding the vocabulary with one virtual token per tool, so no separate retriever module is needed at inference. Single LLM agent, offline-trained then deployed; no online memory growth.
what_is_retrieved: Tools / APIs (each ToolBench RapidAPI endpoint, documented with name, description, parameters). Each tool/API is mapped to a unique virtual vocabulary token, and 'retrieval' means the LLM generating that tool token.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus baked into model parameters: the fixed 47k-API ToolBench pool is virtualized into 47k (precisely 46,985) tool tokens learned during three-stage fine-tuning. Tool knowledge is parametric (embedded in the LLM's vocabulary/weights), not an external vector index queried at test time, and not a growing/episodic memory the agent writes during deployment.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Dual: for retrieval evaluation it is a top-k ranking objective scored by NDCG@1/3/5 (generation can produce a ranked list of tool tokens via constrained beam search). For multi-tool queries (I2 intra-category, I3 intra-collection) the model must generate multiple relevant tool tokens, so it also targets recovery of the relevant tool set within the agent trajectory. Primary reported objective is fixed-k NDCG ranking.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Not a CBR work. If forced to map: [Retrieve: yes - but generative tool-token retrieval, not case retrieval; Reuse: N/A; Revise: N/A; Retain: no]. N/A.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself as generative retrieval / unified tool generation; it does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner and does not describe itself as case-based reasoning.
retrieval_unit: tool-API represented as a single virtual token (under the chosen 'atomic' indexing, each of the 47k tools = exactly one new vocabulary token; embedding initialized as the average of the tool-name subtoken embeddings). Alternative indexings (semantic = tool name subtokens, numeric, hierarchical) make a tool span multiple subtokens.
index_source: Static, offline-induced and parametric: tools come from the fixed ToolBench/RapidAPI corpus (47k APIs); the 'index' is the expanded LLM vocabulary plus weights, created offline via tool memorization + retrieval training. No online/test-time induction; the store is frozen after training (the paper explicitly notes adding new tools is a limitation of generative retrieval, Appendix B).
index_structure_topology: Parametric / flat token vocabulary under atomic indexing (each tool = one independent token, no explicit graph or hierarchy). The paper also studies a HIERARCHICAL indexing variant (recursive Brown-style clustering into a tree, root-to-leaf path encodes a tool) and numeric / semantic variants, but the chosen ToolGen uses flat atomic tokens. No dependency graph; the underlying ToolBench taxonomy (category->tool->API) is not used as a retrieval index.
retriever_type: Generative (tool-as-token): the LLM itself IS the retriever, generating tool tokens via next-token prediction with constrained beam search restricted to the tool-token set. No BM25/dense/learned external retriever in the deployed system (those are baselines).
retriever_learning_signal: Next-token-prediction cross-entropy (supervised fine-tuning), in three stages: (1) tool memorization - predict tool token from its documentation; (2) retrieval training - predict relevant tool token(s) from the user query (the key signal for retrieval); (3) end-to-end agent-tuning on trajectories. No contrastive learning, no RL, no preference signal; learning is teacher-forced generation on ToolBench-derived (query, tool-token) and trajectory data.
query_construction: Raw user query is the input; the model generates tool token(s) directly. In the agent setting the query is consumed within a Thought -> Action -> Arguments conversational template (Agent-Flan-style). No query rewriting, decomposition, or synthetic-query expansion at inference (contrasts with the Re-Invoke and IterFeedback baselines, which do query rewriting / iterative feedback).
query_granularity: Two-level: task-level for the standalone tool-retrieval task (one query -> tool tokens), and step/turn-level in the end-to-end agent (at each iteration the model generates a Thought then an Action tool token conditioned on the trajectory so far).
when_to_retrieve: Retrieval task: one-shot generation per query. Agent task: iterative / per-step - the model generates a tool (Action) token at each agent turn (up to 16 turns / ~5 action rounds + final answer) interleaved with tool feedback, until a 'finish' token or the turn limit.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed/structural schedule driven by the generation template rather than an uncertainty or learned-router signal: the model emits a tool (Action) token whenever the agent paradigm reaches the Action slot after a Thought. There is no token-confidence, attention-uncertainty, or learned complexity classifier deciding whether to retrieve; the LLM autonomously decides which/when tool tokens to generate as part of decoding (and emits 'finish' to stop).
reranking: No separate reranking stage. Ranking emerges directly from constrained beam search over tool tokens (beam scores order the candidate tools for NDCG); no cross-encoder or hierarchy-aware reranker.
retrieved_context_refinement: None in the classic sense (no rerank/distill/compress of retrieved documents, because nothing is retrieved into context). The only post-generation processing is constrained beam search, which masks the output distribution to the valid tool-token set, eliminating out-of-vocabulary/nonexistent tool generation (prevents hallucinated tools).
tool_document_engineering: Tool documentation (name, description, parameters) is used as the INPUT in the tool-memorization stage to teach the model the tool->token mapping; at agent inference the predicted tool token fetches that tool's documentation on demand to generate arguments. No synthetic-query augmentation or expanded summaries or weighted-field embeddings; the token embedding is initialized from the average of tool-name subtoken embeddings (atomic indexing).
index_content_separation: Yes (parametric token-as-index + on-demand documentation): the lightweight retrievable unit is the single tool token; the heavy tool documentation is fetched only after the token is generated (used to produce arguments), a progressive-disclosure pattern that avoids putting tool descriptions in the prompt.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Static parametric tool index (frozen after training); the paper explicitly flags adding/maintaining new tools as a limitation of generative retrieval (Appendix B), suggesting continual training / constrained optimization as future work. Integration protocol is ToolBench/RapidAPI API calling (evaluated via StableToolBench, which uses GPT-4 to simulate failed API responses). No live CRUD auto-sync, no MCP.
tool_dependency_awareness: No explicit inter-tool dependency modeling (no dependency graph, bipartite KG, or dependency-aware reranking). Multi-tool composition is handled implicitly by the autoregressive agent trajectory (generating successive tool tokens conditioned on prior feedback), not by a dependency-aware index. [uncertain]
how_retrieved_used: Latent-token injection + generative invocation: the retrieved tool is the generated virtual token itself (no text injected into the prompt). The token then triggers fetching the tool documentation to generate arguments and execute the call; in pure retrieval mode the generated tokens are the ranked output. Tool knowledge lives in the model's parameters, so retrieval and calling are one generation process.
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved within an autoregressive agent loop (Agent-Flan-style decomposition of ReAct): the model generates Thought (plan p_i) -> Action tool token (Index(d_si)) -> uses fetched docs to produce Arguments c_i -> receives feedback f_i, iterating until 'finish'. Retrieval is fused INTO acting (retrieve-by-generation), so there is no separate plan-then-retrieve or retrieve-then-plan stage and no external tree search/MCTS over retrieval.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-tool-call within a rollout: a tool token is generated once per agent turn, after a Thought and before Arguments, interleaved with environment feedback. Not per-CoT-step-token-level retrieval and not per-answer only.
retrieved_item_representation: Latent / virtual token: the injected item is a single learned vocabulary token standing for the tool (atomic indexing), whose embedding was initialized from the tool name; the corresponding tool documentation is fetched on demand to instantiate the call. Not a raw trajectory, free-text workflow, or executable program-text injected into the prompt.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Procedural tool / executable API endpoint, encoded at the most compact abstraction possible - a single virtual token per tool. The retrieved unit is concrete (one API), not a distilled strategy, workflow, or trajectory.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Constrained beam search / constrained decoding restricts generation to valid tool tokens, guaranteeing zero nonexistent-tool hallucination (vs ToolLlama/GPT-3.5 which hallucinate; ToolLlama >50% nonexistent tool names when no tools are listed in prompt). Atomic indexing also reduces hallucination relative to semantic/numeric/hierarchical indexing (which generate ~7%+ non-tool tokens without constraints). There is no retrieved-context-noise problem because no external documents are placed in the prompt.
memory_type: Parametric / none-explicit: tool knowledge is stored in the LLM's parameters (expanded vocabulary + weights) rather than an external episodic/skill/workflow memory. No retrievable growing memory store.
write_back: False: the system does not write new experiences/cases/skills into any memory store during deployment. All learning happens during offline three-stage fine-tuning; at inference the parameters and tool token set are fixed.
online_growth: No: the tool token set / parametric store is frozen after training and does not grow at deployment. Adding new tools requires retraining/continual training and is explicitly noted as a limitation of the generative-retrieval design (Appendix B).
write_back_trigger: Never (no write-back at inference). The only 'writes' are offline gradient updates during the three training stages (tool memorization, retrieval training, agent-tuning).
failure_experience_usage: Not stored as retrievable memory. Failed agent runs are only handled at inference by a retry mechanism (if the model outputs 'give up' or 'I'm sorry', it is re-prompted to regenerate at higher temperature). No success/failure experiences are retained for future retrieval.
memory_evolution_update: N/A at inference (parametric store is fixed). During training the embeddings/weights are updated via SGD, but there is no append/dedup/forget/link-and-evolve of any retrievable entries post-deployment.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partially: retrieval is realized by a fine-tuned generative model (the LLM learns query->tool-token mapping via supervised next-token prediction), so selection is learned rather than a fixed similarity top-k. However it is NOT an RL- or value-optimized policy (no M-MDP / soft Q-learning / reward signal); it is supervised teacher-forced generation.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No: single-agent, single-model. Tool knowledge is private to the one fine-tuned LLM; there is no cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing.
benchmarks: ToolBench (Qin et al., 2023; 16k+ tool collections, 47k unique APIs) with the standard I1 (single-tool), I2 (intra-category multi-tool), I3 (intra-collection multi-tool) splits for retrieval; StableToolBench (Guo et al., 2024) for end-to-end agent evaluation (solvable-query subset with GPT-4 simulated API outputs).
benchmark_family: tool (ToolBench / RapidAPI tool retrieval and tool-use; StableToolBench for stabilized end-to-end agent evaluation).
baselines: Retrieval task: BM25 (sparse, unsupervised), Long-Context LLM (gpt-4o over ~2k tools incl. ground truth), Embedding Similarity / EmbSim (OpenAI text-embedding-3-large), Re-Invoke (unsupervised query-rewriting + document expansion), IterFeedback (BERT retriever + gpt-3.5-turbo-0125 iterative feedback, up to 10 rounds), ToolRetriever (BERT retriever trained with contrastive learning, the ToolBench retriever). End-to-end task: GPT-3.5 (gpt-3.5-turbo-0613, StableToolBench setup), ToolLlama-2 (Llama-2 fine-tuned on ToolBench), ToolLlama / ToolLlama-3 (Llama-3 fine-tuned on ToolBench, same base model as ToolGen, for fair comparison).
key_metrics: Retrieval: NDCG@1, NDCG@3, NDCG@5 (per domain I1/I2/I3, in-domain and multi-domain). End-to-end: Solvable Pass Rate (SoPR) and Solvable Win Rate (SoWR, vs GPT-3.5 reference), per category and micro-average, each averaged over 3 runs. Also hallucination rate (% generated tools that do not exist) and number of subtokens per tool (efficiency).
headline_result: Tool retrieval: ToolGen (single model) is competitive with the multi-model IterFeedback system and clearly beats ToolRetriever; e.g. In-Domain I2 NDCG@1/3/5 = 91.45/88.79/91.13 (best, beating IterFeedback 89.01/85.46/87.10) and I1 NDCG@5 = 92.67 (best). In the harder Multi-Domain setting ToolGen far exceeds ToolRetriever (e.g. I1 NDCG@1 87.67 vs 72.31; I3 NDCG@1 79.00 vs 52.00). End-to-end: best average SoPR (G.T. 54.19, Retriever 53.28) and SoWR (G.T. 49.70, Retriever 51.51), surpassing GPT-3.5 and ToolLlama while using NO external retriever and zero tool hallucination under constrained decoding.
ablations: Retrieval training-stage ablation (Table 3, Multi-Domain): removing tool memorization causes a minor drop (e.g. I1 NDCG@1 87.67->84.00); removing retrieval training is catastrophic (I1 NDCG@1 87.67->10.17), confirming retrieval training is the key driver; removing constrained beam search barely changes retrieval NDCG (it matters for hallucination, not ranking). Indexing-method comparison (Tables 2 & 5): semantic indexing slightly best for retrieval NDCG, but ATOMIC indexing is best end-to-end (avg SoPR 55.00 vs semantic 51.87, hierarchical 45.50, numeric 35.45) and is most token-efficient (1 token/tool). Hallucination (Fig. 4): ToolGen w/ constrained decoding = 0% nonexistent tools; w/o constraint ~7% (atomic), more for semantic; ToolLlama >50% without tools in prompt. Generalization (Appendix J): tool memorization improves generalization to unseen tools (e.g. train I1 -> test I2 NDCG@1 11.28 w/o vs 40.86 w/ memorization), though end-to-end on unseen tools ToolGen underperforms ToolLlama (weaker task-completion generalization).
evaluation_decoupling: Yes: intrinsic retrieval metrics (NDCG@1/3/5) are reported separately (Section 4) from end-to-end agent task metrics (SoPR/SoWR, Section 5), with dedicated retrieval and end-to-end experimental sections.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Mostly outcome (NDCG ranking quality; SoPR/SoWR task success/win). Some process/diagnostic metrics are reported: tool-hallucination rate (validity of generated actions) and subtokens-per-tool / inference efficiency, but no step-wise reasoning-faithfulness or trajectory-quality scoring.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Efficiency is a central claim: by folding retrieval into generation, ToolGen removes the separate retrieval step (no external retriever calls / no tool descriptions in the prompt), reducing latency and cost. Atomic indexing makes each tool a single token, minimizing the number of generated tokens and inference time vs numeric/semantic/hierarchical indexing (which need multiple subtokens). Trained on 4xA100 (DeepSpeed ZeRO-3): 8 epochs tool memorization + 1 epoch retrieval training; agent context truncated to 6,144, batch size 512, Flash-Attention. No precise latency/throughput numbers are tabulated. [uncertain on exact latency numbers]
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k for retrieval reporting (k=1/3/5 via constrained beam search). For the agent, no tool descriptions occupy the prompt (tool is a single generated token; documentation fetched on demand), context length truncated to 6,144 tokens; up to 16 agent turns (~5 action rounds + final answer) vs ToolLlama's 6-turn limit. Selection count is generation-driven rather than budget-capped retrieval of top-k documents.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (ToolGen does not introduce a new benchmark; it reuses ToolBench and StableToolBench). ToolBench: 16k+ tool collections / 47k unique APIs; retrieval data ~200k (query, relevant-API) pairs split I1/I2/I3 with 87,413 / 84,815 / 25,251 instances; ToolGen's retrieval training ~500k samples and end-to-end training ~183k samples (derived/converted from ToolBench).
builds_on: ToolBench / ToolLLM (Qin et al., 2023) for the 47k-API tool pool, splits, and ToolRetriever/ToolLlama baselines; generative retrieval (DSI / GENRE / Wang et al. 2022; document-identifier generation); ToolkenGPT (Hao et al., 2023, tool-specific tokens) and Toolformer (Schick et al., 2023, vocabulary expansion for a few tools), which ToolGen extends to 47k real-world tools with full-parameter fine-tuning; Agent-Flan (Chen et al., 2024) inference paradigm (separating Thought/Action/Arguments); StableToolBench (Guo et al., 2024) for evaluation; Llama-3-8B base model.
contrasts_with: The standard retriever-then-LLM pipeline (BM25, EmbSim, ToolRetriever dense retriever, IterFeedback, Re-Invoke) that uses a separate encoder retriever and puts tool descriptions in the prompt; ToolkenGPT and Toolformer (few-shot prompting / few tools, still list tools in the prompt) - ToolGen handles 47k tools, requires no tools in the prompt, and uses full-parameter fine-tuning. Argues the pipeline suffers from error propagation, context-length limits, and retriever-LLM misalignment.
lineage: Group E (tool-use). Lineage: generative tool retrieval - reframes the ToolLLM/ToolBench large-scale (47k-API) tool-retrieval problem as next-token generation by virtualizing each tool as a vocabulary token (atomic indexing), unifying retrieval and calling in one LLM with no separate retriever. Bridges generative document retrieval (DSI/GENRE) and tool-token approaches (ToolkenGPT/Toolformer) into a scalable, parametric, end-to-end tool agent; sits alongside dependency-/document-engineering tool-retrieval works (e.g. COLT, AnyTool, ToolRet) but is distinctive as the generative (retriever-free) branch.
